Drive. Don't Ask.
Mumbai. A sea-facing mansion on Malabar Hill. Four hundred guests, a string quartet, and a cake shaped like a cricket trophy.
It's the engagement party of the Mumbai Monarchs' captain. Every player has to attend. Even the rookie from Sonpur who has been in the squad for six days.
My suit is borrowed. My shoes are borrowed. Nobody here knows my name. Time to leave.
11:40 PM. You slip out through the service gate and wave down an auto-rickshaw. As it pulls away, the other door flies open.
A girl in a silver lehenga throws herself onto the seat beside you, kicks off her heels and pulls a dupatta over her hair.
Drive. Don't ask.
Madam, this is HIS auto.
Then he can pay. Drive!
Behind you, two security guards with earpieces run out of the gate, looking left and right. The auto turns the corner.
"Hi. I'm {first}. You're welcome."
Play along.
"Are you in trouble? Should I call the police?"
Worried.
"Get out. I don't need trouble."
You have a career to protect.
I'm not in trouble. I'm escaping trouble. There's a difference.
Charming. Five minutes. Then I'm gone, and you can go back to having no trouble at all.
Marine Drive. The sea is black and the streetlights curve around the bay like a necklace. She hasn't told you her name.
Can I ask you something? Have you ever done one thing in your life that nobody chose for you?
"Left home with forty rupees to play cricket."
The truth.
"Got in this auto. Turned out to be a mistake."
Tease her.
Buy her a vada pav from the last stall still open.
Answer with food.
Forty rupees. I've spent more than that on a straw.
You're the first person tonight who didn't want something from me.
She eats it in four bites, chilli on her silver lehenga, laughing at herself. A real laugh. It changes her whole face.
Best thing I've eaten all year. Don't tell my nutritionist. Don't tell anyone.
You sit on the sea wall until the sky turns pink. At 5:50 AM she stands, picks up her heels, and stops a passing taxi.
Thank you, rookie. Whoever you are. Don't look for me.
Rookie. I never told her I play cricket.
11 AM. Team photo shoot at the stadium. The owner walks in with his family for the season launch. The players straighten up.
Gentlemen. Meet my daughter, Meera. And as you all know, as of last night, our captain's fiancée.
Silver earrings. Same face. Captain Kunal Sethi puts his arm around her waist for the cameras. She smiles like a statue.
Across the room her eyes find yours. For half a second they go wide. Then she very slightly shakes her head.
She's engaged to your captain. And her father signs your contract.
